question: Does training for block-unavailable questionnaire inputs improve stroke-history probability quality beyond fixed-model masking and scenario-specific recalibration?
endpoint: CVDSTRK3 self-reported lifetime stroke history (1=yes,2=no); exclude all other responses
calibration: 2024 dedicated calibration partition; logistic calibration on clipped probability logit; C=1; no external refit
training_weights: unweighted; no resampling or class balancing
mask_training: each fitting/stopping respondent appears in all four predefined scenarios with equal weight; natural nonresponse stays missing; original-variable availability indicators appended

primary.contrast: mask_trained minus fixed_scenario_calibration in Brier loss (negative favors mask training)
primary.seed_combination: average probabilities of three independently fitted seeds for each condition
primary.interval: 95% stratified-PSU Taylor linearization of ratio mean, with-replacement approximation; no finite-population correction; t critical using PSU-minus-strata df; no interval if singleton strata

secondary: unweighted Brier, AUROC, average precision, NLL and ECE
sex, age (18-44/45-64/65+) and income (<35k/35k+) domains where n>=200 and positive>=20
seed ranges; remaining scenarios, families and contrasts exploratory; no multiplicity-adjusted superiority claim
natural_missingness: retain respondents with missing predictors; numeric median imputation and indicators; categorical missing category; fit preprocessing only on fitting data
prohibitions: no future-stroke, clinical-utility or causal claims
no claim that standard mask training, calibration or subset refitting is a novel algorithm
no selection of manuscript headline from secondary comparisons
prior_exposure: 2024 test and 2023 transport outcomes and multiple development pilots already inspected; 2025 official schema/codebook inspected, no predictive evaluation before this protocol
planned_output: IEEE-format empirical research draft; contribution and acceptance remain subject to critical review
